samples.summary: The sticky projection's headline numbers are not stable across arms, contradicting its own "re-derived in full on every update" contract. Only the panel-workflow call sites pass `--max-rounds` and `--required-checks` (agent-review-panel.yml lines ~1004/1274/1441/1753); the CI arm (agent-iterate-ci.yml `ci-paged`, `ci-fix-pushed`), `@claude fix` (`on-demand-fix`) and `@claude rerun` pass neither. So the same comment alternates between `**Fix rounds used:** 2 of 3` and `**Fix rounds used:** 2`, and the count itself is computed over a different check set (full lens manifest vs the guard's `required_checks`) depending on which arm updated last. The stated design property is that a missed/late update self-heals because the body is recomputed; here the recomputation is caller-dependent, so the value flaps rather than converging — on the single surface this change exists to make legible. `MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS` is a literal `"3"` in agent-review-panel.yml:135 and could be passed (or centralised) from the other arms too.

`buildRounds` re-implements the per-commit round grouping that `rounds.mjs::groupReviewRounds` already owns (same `app.slug === "github-actions"` guard, same lens-name filter, same "latest run per lens wins" reduction, same `agent-review-` prefix strip, same oldest-first ordering). The stated reason for a separate function — avoid the per-check-run `output.text` back-fill — only concerns what is extracted from each run, not the grouping rule. The repo's own convention is to share the grouping and vary the projection (cf. `fixAttemptCommits`/`countFailedReviewRounds`). Two copies of "what counts as a round" can drift, and only the guard's copy is covered by rounds.test.mjs's grouping cases.

Third copy of the comment-author trust rule. `rounds.mjs` owns it (`isPagedLatchComment`, plus a module-private `TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS`); loop-status.mjs copies the association set and the bot/association logic into a local `isTrustedAuthor`, and agent-iterate-ci.yml's attempts guard now inlines a fourth literal copy (PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS + TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS + predicate). loop-status.mjs already imports `PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS` from rounds.mjs, so the clean shape is for rounds.mjs to export a marker-independent `isTrustedCommentAuthor(comment)` that both this module and (by literal copy) the workflow mirror. As written the module copy is unpinned against the source of truth, unlike the `gate` job's latch literal which rounds.test.mjs pins byte-for-byte — the discipline the new inline copy's own comment invokes.

The new author-checked paged-latch predicate inlined into agent-iterate-ci.yml's attempts guard has no drift pin. loop-status.test.mjs pins only the `CI_PAGED_LATCH` string against the workflow; nothing asserts that the workflow's inline `PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS`/`TRUSTED_ASSOCIATIONS`/predicate still match `rounds.mjs`. This is exactly the failure mode rounds.mjs:34-39 documents for the `gate` job (a drifted copy does not error, it silently stops latching) and which rounds.test.mjs guards there.

The task doc's job-summary item asks for `session-job-summary.mjs` "turns/tokens/cost/outcome per Claude session", and the implement, CI-fix and review-fix arms all get one — but the on-demand `@claude fix` session (agent-fix.yml, which already stages agent-tools and records a metrics ledger entry at line 426) gets only a loop-status update, no session job summary. Either add the step for symmetry or note in the doc why the standalone `agent-fix-effort` comment is considered sufficient for that arm.

`guard-verdict.mjs` exports a reusable fail-safe `appendStepSummary(md)`, yet panel-job-summary.mjs (line 152) and session-job-summary.mjs (line 90) each re-implement the identical read-env/appendFileSync/try-catch block. Importing the existing helper would keep one definition of "how this repo writes a step summary".

Placement: the new Phase 21 prose is appended AFTER the phase's "Done criteria:" line, so the section now reads deliverables → done criteria → two more delivered items. The Phase 21 deliverable list already has a **Delivered** annotation convention (line 356); folding the loop-status projection in as a deliverable bullet (or placing the prose before "Done criteria") would match it.

verdict.reason: Every factual claim checks out. loop-status.mjs renders the budget line as `**Fix rounds used:** ${failed}${max !== null ? ' of ' + max : ''}` (:251-258), with `max` coming only from `--max-rounds` (:410) and the counted set from `--required-checks` with a fallback to the full lens manifest (:365-368, :386-390). Only the panel arm supplies those flags (agent-review-panel.yml:1014-1019, 1284-1287, 1447-1451, 1764-1767; the stalled path at :1996-2000 supplies only --max-rounds). The CI arm (agent-iterate-ci.yml:235-237, 440-441), `@claude fix` (agent-fix.yml:536-539) and `@claude rerun` (agent-rerun.yml:234-237) supply neither, so the same sticky comment alternates between `N of 3` and bare `N` and can count over a different check set depending on which arm updated last. MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS is a workflow-local literal "3" (agent-review-panel.yml:135), inaccessible to the other arms. This contradicts the module's own stated projection contract (loop-status.mjs:1-11) and the design doc's framing (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:370-385) on the one surface the task file (docs/tasks/active/20260806-agent-loop-observability-todo.md:14-22, 35-36) exists to make legible. The in-code comment at :246-250 and the doc's "when the caller passes it" acknowledge the caller-dependence but do not guard against the flapping, so no refutation ground (not-present / already-guarded / out-of-scope) applies.
